subject: botany_2
question_text: List out the beneficial aspects of transgenic plants.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.35, printed question 45. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: the insider note said a benefit without a named plant is half a point, which asserts a mark outcome this card does not hold and devalues NCERT's own unnamed benefits such as increased efficiency of mineral usage, so it now asks for the named crops without claiming a mark.

insider_note: Five headings, each with a named crop. Bt cotton, Flavr Savr and golden rice are the three names to be sure of — naming the crop for each heading makes the answer complete.

steps.label: Resistance to pests and pathogens
steps.margin_note: All four examples with crop and pathogen. This heading alone is a full mark.
lines: (i) Transgenic PAPAYA is resistant to papaya
(ii) BT COTTON is resistant to insects, chiefly
steps.why: One transgene can replace repeated spraying, so the benefit is measured in pesticide not used as much as in yield gained.
common_mistakes: Naming benefits with no crops. Each example needs its plant AND its pest.
Saying Bt cotton resists viruses. It resists INSECTS.
steps.memory_tip: Four crops, four different enemies: virus, insect, bacterium, fungus.

steps.label: Food processing
steps.margin_note: Name the variety, the property, and why it matters.
lines: The transgenic tomato FLAVR SAVR is bruise
resistant, because its ripening is DELAYED.
So it can be stored and transported without
steps.why: A tomato that ripens slowly can be picked ripe and still survive transport, which is what makes delayed ripening commercially useful.
common_mistakes: Saying Flavr Savr ripens faster. Its ripening is DELAYED.
Not naming the variety. Flavr Savr is the named example.
steps.memory_tip: Delayed ripening means it survives the journey.

steps.label: Nutritional value
steps.margin_note: The crop, the compound, and the deficiency it prevents.
lines: GOLDEN RICE, developed from the Taipei rice
variety, is rich in beta-carotene, the
It helps prevent blindness caused by vitamin A
steps.why: Rice grain normally carries no beta-carotene at all, so adding the pathway addresses a deficiency in the crop people already eat.
common_mistakes: Saying golden rice contains vitamin A itself. It contains BETA-CAROTENE, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Not saying what deficiency it addresses. Blindness from vitamin A deficiency is the point.
steps.memory_tip: Golden because of the carotene, and carotene becomes vitamin A.

steps.label: Hybrid seed and stress tolerance
steps.margin_note: Both remaining headings with their named crops. Five headings in total.

lines.text: easier to breed, and stress tolerant

lines: MALE STERILE plants of Brassica napus remove the
need for manual emasculation, and so cut the
The BASMATI rice variety was made resistant to
steps.why: Emasculating flowers by hand is the single most expensive step in hybrid seed production, so a male sterile plant removes the cost rather than reducing it.
common_mistakes: Leaving out male sterility. It is one of the five named headings.
Saying herbicide tolerance kills weeds. It lets the CROP survive the herbicide that kills the weeds.
steps.memory_tip: Male sterile means no hand emasculation, and that is where the money is.
